question.problem:
A math test is composed of $15$ exercises. The time that a student takes to solve an exercise, in minutes, is normally distributed with a mean of $6\,\text{min}$ and a standard deviation of $2\,\text{min}.$ If one student is randomly selected, what is the probability that they will take between $80\,\text{min}$ and $100\,\text{min}$ to complete all exercises? You may assume that the times spent solving each exercise are mutually independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8554\,$ | $\,0.8577\,$ | $\,0.8599\,$ | $\,0.8621\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8770\,$ | $\,0.8790\,$ | $\,0.8810\,$ | $\,0.8830\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8962\,$ | $\,0.8980\,$ | $\,0.8997\,$ | $\,0.9015\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{i}$ denote the time spent solving the $i$th exercise. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(60,{2}^{2}),\,1\le i\le 15.
$$

Let the random variable $W$ denote the time it takes a randomly selected student to complete the test. Then, since

$$
W={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{15},
$$

we have that $W$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[W] & =15\cdot 6 \\  & =90, \\ \text{Var}[W] & =15\cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
W∼N(90,60).
$$

In order to find $P(80<W<100),$ we convert $W$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(80<W<100) & =P(\frac{80-90}{\sqrt{60}}<Z<\frac{100-90}{\sqrt{60}}) \\  & ≈P(-1.29<Z<1.29) \\  & =Φ(1.29)-Φ(-1.29) \\  & =Φ(1.29)-(1-Φ(1.29)) \\  & =2Φ(1.29)-1\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(1.29)≈0.9015.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(80<W<100) & ≈2Φ(1.29)-1 \\  & ≈0.8030.\end{aligned}
$$
